A poor scanned, image-only PDF blocks go-live because the ingestion pipeline fails to extract any text layer. The standard PDF parser cannot detect text in image-only documents, leading to empty document models or incomplete text extraction [NL-029][NL-010]. Because the KnowledgeHub expects an embedded text layer before ingestion, it cannot index the text or generate citation anchors for these files [NL-018].

Without citation anchors, TutorChat either returns answers with no source citations (unable to find text offsets) or points to the entire document (e.g., page 1 of a 250-page PDF) instead of the exact section [NL-021]. This directly violates the reliability guidelines and is the largest ticket category, accounting for 112 of 412 support tickets (27%) in May 2026 [NL-021].

In enterprise accounts, the workaround is manual OCR pre-processing by the customer or CS team, which adds weeks to onboarding (e.g., Northstar Financial delayed by three weeks; a clinical account was stuck onboarding for 9 weeks after ingesting only a third of its library) [NL-010][NL-018]. This ultimately fails the reliability gate: the go-live validation threshold requires 85% citation correctness, and scanned PDFs return incomplete citations, failing that threshold [NL-031]. As a result, compliance officers refuse to sign off, and deployment remains blocked—BrightPath was restricted to a 100-user pilot and could not expand to its full 6,500 employees [NL-021].
